claims.excerpt:
add:
            fügt etwas (meist einen vector) hinzu, auch wenns den eintrag bereits gibt.
            wenn der Path zb Path="/Values/Trader/Progression, dann sollte der vector nicht mit Progression anfangen, außer man will tatsächlich einen zweiten Progression Vector haben. Aber stattdessen will man ja eher dem Progression Ast etwas zufügen.
            ich denke "add" sollte man vermeiden, weil es einen eintrag doppelt zufügt, sollten die devs oder andere mods den eintrag ebenfalls zufügen.
            besser wäre da also replace, wenn man sicher sein will, dass der eigene mod funktioniert.
            noch besser wäre aber natürlich ein merge_add Befehl, um sowohl die eigenen dinge zuzufügen, als auch bereits vorhandene zu seiner eigenen version zu ändern.

claims.excerpt: All shared mods are intended to not be changed from other modders except the author/s. So you copy paste the desired shared mod into your mod folder, which will automatically enable the shared mod together with your mod. If you want to make iprovements to any shared mod, do a PR to this repository. If you want to change things/texts that are not suited for everyone, do this within your own mod instead, by loading your mod after my shared mod and then do ModOp changes like usual to it.
claims.interpretation: Keep shared copies unmodified; propose shared improvements upstream and apply private integration changes from the consuming mod in a defined later order.

claims.excerpt:
local EventOnObjectDeletionConfirmed = {}
  -- add your function which should be called to the list EventOnObjectDeletionConfirmed with ModID of your mod as key.
  local function _OnObjectDeletionConfirmed(GUID)
    for modname,fn in pairs(EventOnObjectDeletionConfirmed) do
      if type(fn)=="function" then
        local status,err = xpcall(fn,g_LTL_Serp.log_error,GUID)
        if status==false then
          g_LTL_Serp.modlog("ERROR in _OnObjectDeletionConfirmed for mod '"..tostring(modname).."': "..tostring(err),ModID)
        end
      end
claims.interpretation: Register under your own ModID in the provided callback map; do not replace the whole shared map.

claims.excerpt:
local incompatible_logs = SearchModLog_Pnski("is incompatible with:")
    -- print(incompatible_logs)
    for linenumber,line in pairs(incompatible_logs) do
      if linenumber > last_modsloaded_linenumber then
        local inc_mod1,inc_mod2 = string.match(line,".*%] (.*) is incompatible with: .*%] (.*)") -- eg. "[2024-08-15 22:35:39.877] [error] [Gameplay] testmod is incompatible with: shared_IncompatibleModsPopUp"
        if inc_mod2==nil then -- eg if it does not have a Category in brackets (mod1 always has brackets in front, eg [error])
          inc_mod1,inc_mod2 = string.match(line,".*%] (.*) is incompatible with: (.*)")
        end
        -- print(inc_mod1,inc_mod2)
        if inc_mod1~=nil and inc_mod2~=nil then
          table.insert(inc_mods_list,{inc_mod1,inc_mod2}) -- inc_mod1 is a ModName, while inc_mod2 is a ModID
claims.interpretation: The helper reads incompatibility messages already present in the loader log; it cannot prove absence of undisclosed logical conflicts.

claims.excerpt: <ModOp Type="remove" Path="//Asset[Values/Standard/GUID='1500010714'][position() & last()]"/>
claims.interpretation: This expression has an invalid XPath operator. It is not copied as a usable recipe; retain the existing discrepancy record.
Add appends payload nodes; it does not check for an identically named existing container.
Recursive merge matches repeated names by occurrence, recurses into existing children and appends missing nodes. An empty payload child does not clear descendants.
For a shared ModID the older version is skipped; equal-version/different-content copies are not a compatibility contract.
Normal and load-last mods are ordered in separate graphs; phase boundaries matter in addition to named dependencies.

survey.pattern: compatib|kompatib|add the path if|does not replace|another mod|not overwrite
survey.boundary: Keyword hits identify candidates, not authorship or completed reviews. Identical bundles retain their paths; selected snippets are attributed individually. JSON inventories/metadata are not treated as prose claims.

reproduction.baseline: Full effective XML generated before editing this patch; receipt hashes verify the captured input.

limits: Add is not made generally idempotent. Existing duplicate containers are not repaired.
No broad rewrite of merchant/story/helper mods; they remain original evidence.
No game, MP, save migration, publication or kit synchronization.
This new chapter/current patch is not included in its baseline GitHub links.
